title: Presheaf fibers of a relative left cone
statement:
Use quasicategories, spaces, coherent functor categories, equivalences and homotopy pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and space-valued right-fibration classification from [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ and write $\mathcal S$ for $\mathcal U$-small spaces. Let $p:E\to A$ be any functor of $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories. Form the simplicial pushout $D=A\amalg_{E\times\{0\}}(E\times\Delta^1)$, with inclusion $j:A\to D$, and put $\mathcal P(T)=\operatorname{Fun}(T^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. The restriction $j^*:\mathcal P(D)\to\mathcal P(A)$ is a Cartesian fibration. For $X\in\mathcal P(A)$, choose its small right fibration $r_X:Y_X\to A$ and put $E_X=E\times_A Y_X$. There are equivalences of infinity categories
$$\mathcal P(D)_X\simeq\mathcal P(E)_{/p^*X}\simeq\mathcal P(E_X).$$
Here the first category is the infinity-categorical fiber with its specified identification of the restriction with $X$; the middle category is the coherent slice, including homotopies over $p^*X$. A presheaf $\phi$ corresponds first to $\Psi=\phi|_{E\times\{1\}}$ with the coherent transformation $\Psi\to p^*X$ supplied by its cylinder data, and then to the presheaf
$$\widetilde\Psi(e,y)=\operatorname{fib}_{y}\bigl(\Psi(e)\to X(p(e))\bigr).$$
The equivalences include transformations and all higher simplices. They are natural in $p$, and in $X$ contravariantly: for $h:X'\to X$, Cartesian transport in the first and middle descriptions is $\Psi\mapsto\Psi\times_{p^*X}p^*X'$, while in the last description it is restriction along $E_{X'}\to E_X$. All fibers and pullbacks in these equivalences are homotopy fibers and infinity-categorical pullbacks; for the chosen right-fibration models the displayed simplicial pullbacks represent them. Presheaf categories are formed in containing universes.

source.place: GHN Definition 9.1, Lemma 9.4, Remark 9.5, Proposition 9.6 and Corollary 9.8, including the explicit fiber formula in the proof of Proposition 9.12. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text:
Put $C=\mathcal P(E)$ and $B=\mathcal P(A)$. The pushout defining $D$ gives an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\mathcal P(D)\cong B\times_{p^*,C,t}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C),\qquad t=\operatorname{ev}_1.$$
Indeed, an $n$-simplex on the left is a map $D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S$. It is exactly a pair of maps on $A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ and $(E\times\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ agreeing on $(E\times\{0\})^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$. Reverse the cylinder interval and curry the second map: this is an arrow in $C$ whose target is $p^*$ of the first map. Its source is restriction to the original endpoint $1$. Operators are precomposition on $\Delta^n$, so the same description holds for transformations and every higher simplex. This is just the internal-Hom definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the degreewise pushout universal property. In particular no claim that $D$ itself is a quasicategory is needed.

source.place: Definition 9.1 and the pullback calculation in the proof of Lemma 9.4, after taking opposites

proof.text: The categories $B,C$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $C$ has pullbacks computed in spaces at each vertex of $E$. Apply [lem-coef-arrow-target-cartesian-pullbacks] to $C$. Under step 1, $j^*$ is the base change of $t$ along $p^*$. The inner-horn and Cartesian-edge horn lifting problems for this base change are the same problems for $t$ with the base simplex fixed by $p^*$, so the lifts remain in the pullback. Each required lift into a chosen target exists there. Thus [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] gives a Cartesian fibration $j^*$. The lift over $h:X'\to X$ is the square obtained by pulling $\Psi\to p^*X$ back to $p^*X'$; its source presheaf is $\Psi\times_{p^*X}p^*X'$.

source.place: Remark 9.5, Cartesian part; pointwise existence of pullbacks in presheaves

proof.text: Taking the degreewise fiber of step 1 at $X$ gives the target-fixed arrow category $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_C\{p^*X\}$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] to $C$ and its vertex $p^*X$: the join-defined coherent slice $C_{/p^*X}$ is equivalent to this arrow fiber over $C$. This identifies the first fiber with the asserted slice, not just with its objects or its core. The arrow is precisely $\Psi\to p^*X$ from step 1. The fixed-target evaluation is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to $\{1\}\subset\Delta^1$ and $C\to *$; the same holds for its base change $j^*$. The final step below verifies that these strict fibers present fibers with a specified equivalence to $X$.

source.place: Lemma 9.4 and Remark 9.5, identification of the fixed-target fiber

proof.text: Write $Y=E_X$ and $r:Y\to E$. By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], base change of $r_X$ classifies $F=p^*X$; it is small. Denote the contravariant simplicial model category on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/E}$ by $M_E$, as in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Composition with $r$ identifies the underlying ordinary category $\mathrm{sSet}_{/Y}$ with $(\mathrm{sSet}_{/E})_{/r}$, by forgetting only a redundant composite. Compare the contravariant model $M_Y$ with the slice model $M_E/r$ of [lem-coef-model-over-structure]. Both have monomorphisms as cofibrations. A fibrant object of the second is $q:Z\to Y$ which is an $M_E$-fibration. Its composite to $E$ is fibrant, and [lem-coef-contravariant-fibrations-between-right-fibrations] says exactly that $q$ is a right fibration. Conversely a right fibration $q$ has right-fibration composite $rq$ (compose horn lifts), so that same criterion makes it $M_E$-fibrant over $r$. These are precisely the fibrant objects of $M_Y$. Therefore [lem-coef-model-structure-determined-by-fibrant-objects] identifies the two model structures, including their weak equivalences, under this ordinary-category identification.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 9.7: comparison of the two model structures

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal R_E$ be the ordinary category of small right fibrations over $E$, with weak equivalences and fibrations inherited from $M_E$. It satisfies the Brown hypotheses: its terminal object is $1_E$, pullbacks and compositions of (trivial) fibrations are inherited from the model lifting classes, and model factorization of a map to a fibrant object has fibrant middle object. All objects of $M_E$ are cofibrant by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Hence [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] and [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] make the classification functor $q_E:N\mathcal R_E\to\mathcal P(E)$ an infinity localization: its universal property is unchanged on postcomposing with an equivalence, since postcomposition with the quasi-inverse gives inverse equivalences of the functor categories in that property. Put $F_0=q_E(r)$, with the classification identification $F_0\simeq F=p^*X$. Apply [lem-coef-brown-slice-fraction-calculus] directly to this localization:
$$L(\mathcal R_E(r))\simeq\mathcal P(E)_{/F_0}.$$
Step 4 identifies $\mathcal R_E(r)$, including weak equivalences, with right fibrations over $Y$. The same model-localization and classification statements identify its localization with $\mathcal P(Y)$. Postcomposition with $F_0\simeq F$ identifies the displayed slice with $\mathcal P(E)_{/F}$: postcompose with its inverse for the reverse functor, and the two inverse homotopies give the natural equivalences of their composites to the identity. The resulting equivalence sends $q:Z\to Y$ to $rq:Z\to E$ with its arrow to $r$, because the Brown comparison is induced by $q_E$ on slices. Thus triangle homotopies and all mapping spaces are retained.

source.place: Proposition 9.7 and Corollary 9.8, with the existing Brown slice comparison supplying the coherent-slice step

proof.text:
To compute the inverse in step 5, represent $\Psi\to F$ by a fibrant slice object $q:Z\to Y$ in $M_E/r$. This is legitimate for every coherent slice object by step 5, not an assertion that an arbitrary map of right fibrations is already a right fibration. By step 4, $q$ is a right fibration. Classification [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies $Z_e$ with $\Psi(e)$, $Y_e$ with $X(p(e))$, and the map $Z_e\to Y_e$ with the component of $\Psi\to F$. Pullback of $q$ to $Y_e$ is a right fibration over a Kan complex. By [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] it is a Kan fibration, and its strict fiber at $y$ is naturally equivalent to its homotopy fiber. On the other hand, classification over $Y$ evaluates the presheaf represented by $q$ at $(e,y)$ as precisely this strict fiber. Thus
$$\widetilde\Psi(e,y)\simeq\operatorname{fib}_{y}(\Psi(e)\to X(p(e))).$$
The cited natural fiber comparison applies to entire simplicial maps, so this computes the transformation and higher-simplex data as well as the values.

source.place: Explicit fiber calculation in the proof of Proposition 9.12

proof.text: Represent $h:X'\to X$ by a map $Y_{X'}\to Y_X$ over $A$, using the mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], and let $g:Y'=E_{X'}\to Y=E_X$ be its pullback. For $q:Z\to Y$ as in step 6, restriction of its classified presheaf along $g$ is classified by $Z\times_Y Y'\to Y'$. Its composite to $E$ represents the pullback of $\Psi\to F$ along $F'=p^*X'\to F$: indeed $q$ is a fibration between fibrant objects of $M_E$ by step 4, and [lem-coef-brown-fibrant-localization-pullbacks] sends its ordinary pullback square to a pullback square in $L\mathcal R_E$. Classification identifies the latter with the desired presheaf pullback, computed pointwise by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. This agrees with step 2. For a commuting square between two functors $p$, restriction along the two base maps takes the cylinder pair of step 1 to its restricted pair, and takes $Z\to E\times_A Y_X$ to the corresponding base change. The naturality under base change, composition and higher simplices in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] makes these comparisons coherent. Pullback associativity identifies successive restrictions with restriction along a composite; the Brown pullback comparison is natural for maps of squares. These are functors and equivalences on whole categories, so they prove the stated naturality, rather than only a pointwise correspondence.

source.place: Naturality clauses of Proposition 9.7, Corollary 9.8 and Proposition 9.6

proof.text: Finally verify the geometric meaning of the strict pullbacks. A right fibration $v:V\to T$ of quasicategories is an isofibration: restrict it to the core $T^\simeq$, which is Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The restriction is a right fibration over a Kan complex, hence a Kan fibration with Kan total space by [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber]. It lifts an equivalence of $T$ with any specified source; its lift is an equivalence because every edge of a Kan complex is an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. Inner horn lifts already come from $v$. By [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] this is a Joyal fibration. The fibrant objects of the Joyal model structure [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], with its fibrations and weak equivalences, satisfy the Brown hypotheses just verified for a model category in step 5. Apply [lem-coef-brown-fibrant-localization-pullbacks] in this category: pullbacks along these fibrations present infinity-categorical pullbacks. This applies to $E\times_A Y_X$ and to pullbacks of the right-fibration models. It also applies to the fiber of $j^*$, since step 3 makes it an isofibration. Consequently the strict models used above represent the specified infinity-categorical fibers and pullbacks. The bases $A,E$, the right-fibration representatives and their contravariant-model factorizations stay in $\mathcal U$. Presheaf categories, their Joyal-model comparisons, and categories of model objects are placed in containing universes.

source.place: GHN Proposition 9.6 and its proof: homotopy-invariant interpretation of the right-fibration pullbacks
